text:
zoe: Nimbus legal looped procurement. They want a 3-week technical pilot showing live claim extraction into their case UI. Must include streaming partial results, function/tool calls to their extractor, SOC2 answers, and a short reserved-price estimate. Can we assemble a minimal dev handoff + pricing blurb?
amar: Stack: TypeScript frontend (WS preferred), Python workers, tiny Go ingress. Also will need an example ingest CSV -> streaming flow.
lee: I can draft a tiny end-to-end example (TS + Py). Quick TS pattern for websocket + function_call: 
```ts
const s = client.wsStream({model:'redwood-medium', structured_output:true, tools:['claim_extract']});
s.on('function_call', async (c)=>{ const ok = await fetch('/adapter/extract',{method:'POST', body:JSON.stringify({text:c.args.text})}); const res = await ok.json(); await s.resume({tool_result:res}); });
```
Use SSE if they can't do WS; SSE will still stream function_call + tool_result events.
rachel: Ops notes: for a short pilot set batch_size=1, max_concurrency=3, prefix_kv_cache=true for reused policy docs, and cap token_window=4096. If they want lower latency use the quantized runtime; expect a small quality delta. For production-facing SLOs we recommend dedicated reserved nodes.
owen: Security/procurement checklist I will prep for SOC2 packet: data residency (region list), retention defaults (we keep logs 30d by default), KMS/CMEK options, subprocessors, and ingestion redaction guidance. If they intend to send PII/PHI we should push Redwood Private (VPC) for the pilot. Need their security contact + example payloads (headers OK).
hannah: Pricing sketch: for a 3-week reserved bucket sized for ~1.5 qps sustained (small model) propose $4,500 reserved + list-rate overage; offer a one-time 20% pilot discount and a $500 testing credit. Audit/log-retention beyond 30d billed as add-on. If they ask for dedicated GPU sizes or longer-term reserved terms, we escalate to deal desk.
zoe: Can we confirm the WS vs SSE tradeoffs for live form partial-fill? They want each form field to appear as it is parsed.
lee: WS allows bidirectional low-latency for adapter-driven mid-stream updates. SSE is one-way from server -> client, but it's sufficient if adapter returns quickly and we call /streams/resume with the tool_result. Pattern is: model emits function_call event -> adapter called -> adapter posts tool_result to resume endpoint -> stream emits structured JSON deltas. That gets the UI partial-fill behavior without requiring a persistent WS for every client.
amar: Small gotcha: when mixing structured_output + function_call ensure the extractor's output keys match the schema exactly. Recommend server-side JSON schema validation and a UI fallback to show raw text if schema fails.
owen: I'll also attach a short KMS note: for pilot we can use Redwood-managed keys; if they need customer-managed keys (CMEK) that's a configuration step and may add 2-3 days and a small fee.
rachel: Draft runbook fragment (pasteable):
POC_RUNBOOK:
- env: set REDWOOD_API_KEY, REGION=us-east-1
- start_stream: curl -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-medium" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"input":"<claim text>","structured_output":true}'
- on_function_call: POST /internal/extract -> adapter returns JSON -> POST /streams/resume {"tool_result": <json>}
- runtime: batch_size=1, max_concurrency=3, token_window=4096, prefix_kv_cache=true, fallback=smaller-model
- observability: include X-TRACE header; set log level warn for pilot

hannah: I'll turn the pricing sketch into a one-page blurb + short SOW and send to Zoe by EOD.
zoe: Action items: Lee -> TS + Py snippets and CSV->stream sample; Amar -> confirm WS vs SSE examples and a small sample adapter; Owen -> prefilled SOC2 answers + list of customer inputs required; Hannah -> pricing + 1p SOW; Rachel -> ops runbook final. Target: customer-ready package in 24h. :thumbsup:
redwood-bot: Please tag this thread with #poc-handovers when assets are uploaded so sales-ops can queue onboarding tasks.
zoe: Thanks team, I'll loop in Nimbus once we have the bundle.
